A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Llama3 self-recognition and vector-steering study. The main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. v2 retains Appendices A.1–A.9 and adds A.10–A.12.

before.justification: v1 reports original self-recognition experiments, activation analyses, steering interventions, and vector-removal tests, including numerical results and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Sonnet 3.5 recognition results, context-removal experiments, and comparisons of vectors extracted from separate datasets.

M1.justification: Contrastive activation averaging, nuisance-vector projection, normalization, output steering, and input coloring remain unchanged. Section 2.2 clarifies their implementation; Appendix A.12 explicitly applies the same extraction process separately to existing datasets.

E1.justification: CNN-DailyMail, XSUM, DOLLY, SAD, and Quora QA remain the data sources. Appendix A.11 adds a recognition scenario without source passages, continuation prefixes, questions, or original generation instructions, extending input conditions within the existing tasks.

E2.justification: Sonnet 3.5 is newly evaluated as a recognizer and explicitly compared with Llama3 in the Discussion. Figure 14 tests its discrimination against human, Llama3-8b-chat, and Llama3-8b-base writing. The original comparison sets in Figures 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce Sonnet 3.5 evaluation, context-free Yes/No recognition prompts, and separate dataset-derived vectors compared through layer-16 penultimate-token cosine similarity and Tuned Lens readouts. These supplement the existing protocols; the original accuracy definitions and stated sample counts are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.11 adds a focused ablation of generation context, testing whether recognition persists from the text alone. Appendix A.12 examines sensitivity to the dataset used for vector extraction. These extend the existing confound controls and robustness analyses without replacing them.

E5.justification: Both versions report p-values, confidence intervals, and plotted error bars. The new results continue these reporting practices without introducing a new uncertainty procedure, repeated-run count, or seed disclosure.

E6.justification: Original recognition and steering results are retained. Added results include Sonnet accuracies of 95.5%, 78.3%, and 95.4% against human, Llama3-chat, and Llama3-base writing; context-free XSUM, SAD, and QA accuracies of 40.6%, 65.6%, and 62.3%; and cross-dataset vector similarities of 0.49–0.90. These are supplementary outcomes under added models or conditions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The existing vector operations remain conceptually unchanged, and the added cosine-similarity measurements are empirical diagnostics rather than new mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims about Llama3 self-recognition and causal steering. The concluding Discussion modestly broadens applicability claims to larger and non-Llama models and states that the new Sonnet experiment indicates stronger recognition ability.

C2.justification: Appendix A.11 newly explains recognition failures on short context-free summaries and interprets XSUM results as evidence that context can override surface judgments. Appendix A.12 interprets weaker SAD vector similarity. The Discussion adds specific hypotheses about preventing injected fake responses and monitoring authorship-related activations.

D1.justification: v2 specifies unit-length normalization, pre-output nuisance activations, projection at each layer and position, and character-based trimming. Appendix A.11 supplies the new recognition prompt. These improve procedural documentation, although v1's explicit description of the ten-token extraction span is shortened.

R1.justification: v2 adds Anil et al. on many-shot jailbreaking and connects that work to a proposed safety application. The broader research positioning is retained. Consolidating the duplicate Activation Addition references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology and prose corrections, clarifies vector construction and steering, adds a results recap, and expands the Discussion. The main section sequence and most existing appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 improves plot-label wrapping, arranges Figure 2 horizontally, transposes Figure 4's axes, relocates some displays, and expands explanatory captions. Figures 14–15 and Tables 5–6 are added. These are localized presentation changes within the retained document design.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful checks absent from v1: context removal exposes limits on short-summary recognition, separate-dataset extraction tests vector consistency, and Sonnet adds evidence beyond Llama3. Clearer procedural descriptions and captions also help assessment. The gains are bounded: the steering mechanism remains studied in Llama3, Sonnet's experimental details are sparse, and the proposed jailbreak defenses remain untested hypotheses.
